title: How far must the law reach?
description: Conceptual projection by the unit of obligation and its temporal reach. The law, not file count, determines placement. This tests why a local fact may not entail an end-to-end conclusion.

tl.name: Threads
tl.description: Follow one logical object or operation through movement or repetition. Threads here means continuity of identity, not OS threads. Deduplication widens right when it must cover external participants.

tr.name: Conversations
tr.description: Several histories need a justified relation: effects and acknowledgments, revocation and active sessions, or inspected code and a changing deployment. Recognition alone does not cause the consumer to act.

bl.name: Specimens
bl.description: The focal claim is one value-transfer or admission relation at a boundary. Inspecting a specimen does not make a sampled test universal; the declared domain still matters.

br.name: Assemblies
br.description: One execution has a property only when its reads, writes, transforms, or handles compose correctly. Several files can implement one participant; one process can contain several participants.

examples.label: F16 Stable object targeting
examples.plotReason: Prototype: same object remains the target while list positions change.
examples.note: Stronger temporal claim than preserving a key in one serialized result.

examples.label: F15 Scoped deduplication
examples.plotReason: Boundary case: single-service repeat tolerance can widen into a cross-participant claim.
examples.note: Single-service scope is the plotted transfer hypothesis. Atomicity, retention, and effect domains need evidence. This does not authorize retries.

examples.label: F14 Ack includes effects
examples.plotReason: Prototype: client settlement depends on causal correspondence across histories.
examples.note: Source contract/example; replication and rebase remain outside Endpoints scope. A row ID may not identify an operation.

examples.label: F17 Active-session revocation
examples.plotReason: Different history law: a later policy change needs a response from active consumers.
examples.note: An entry-time check does not itself create a disconnect or revalidation path.

examples.label: F18 Deployment applicability
examples.plotReason: Meta-level outlier: applicability of evidence has its own changing premises.
examples.note: Near both watersheds. Source hash, mutable name, configuration, and database authority are distinct bindings.

examples.label: F08 Lossy key conversion
examples.plotReason: Prototype: an exact value relation can fail within one transfer.
examples.note: An encode/decode pair is one logical value law here; injectivity and ordering remain separate requirements.

examples.label: F06 Transaction handle flow
examples.plotReason: Prototype: a local-looking call joins multiple effect participants.
examples.note: The observation boundary is one transaction execution. Inspection does not add rollback to an escaped participant.

examples.label: F12 One logical snapshot
examples.plotReason: Counterexample to equating composition with missing knowledge: an executor may still be needed.
examples.note: The contract joins reads within one logical execution. A transaction contains internal events; this axis is observational scope, not event count.

calibration.axisClaimType: Conceptual. Framework contracts and generated cases are distinct provenance categories. Coordinates express claim scope, not measured participant counts or durations.
calibration.secondAxisConfidence: Moderate. The observational boundary must be explicit: transactions contain histories and transfers have two ends. Both candidate maps share one fresh agent context.
calibration.orthogonality: Useful off-diagonal cases: stable object targeting is a one-unit history; transaction participation joins several parts within one execution. More history often adds participants, creating diagonal pull. F18 deliberately tests the broader evidence-applicability reading.
